articles.title: Researchers Claim Two RCE Exploits That Bypass Telegram’s New Android Defenses
articles.summary: A malicious widget can bypass the security filter that Telegram added to its Android app last week and run code outside it, according to NebuSec, a security company. Widgets are small interactive blocks that bots send inside chat messages, and their JavaScript runs on the user's phone. The researchers ran their demonstration on a Telegram test server, because only approved bots can send

articles.title: Oracle to Patch 11 Java Flaws Today as Critical OpenJDK RCE (CVE-2026-114938) Report Emerges
articles.summary: Oracle is preparing to release security patches for 11 vulnerabilities in Java SE on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, all of which may be exploited remotely without authentication, as separate reports warn of a potentially critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw affecting OpenJDK. The 11 vulnerabilities carry a maximum CVSS 3.1 severity score of 8.1, according to Oracle's advance security notice.

articles.title: Trigram Campaign Impersonates About 50 AI and Blockchain Brands to Target Devs with Infostealers
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and logistics sectors across Europe and the U.S. have emerged as the target of a large-scale, industrialized campaign dubbed Trigram. "Trigram is a large-scale campaign that impersonates about 50 brands in the blockchain and AI sectors, to trick developers into executing an infostealer themselves," Stormshield said in a deep-dive technical report

articles.summary: Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, known as SHA pinning, has become the go-to defense against software supply chain attacks. Attackers have already found a way around it. In March 2026, the hackers who hijacked Trivy, a widely used open-source security scanner, planted malicious code that looked like it came from GitHub's official checkout tool. articles.title: Researchers Detail iPhone Flaw That Let Apps Record Audio Despite Denied Microphone Permission
articles.summary: A now-patched flaw in Apple's audio service let apps on iPhones and iPads record audio even after the user tapped "Don't Allow" on the microphone prompt. The first security updates with the fix came out on August 17. Neither Apple nor the two researchers who found the flaw report that it was used in attacks. Nik Tsytsarkin of Meta Red Team X published the technical details last week. Mustafa

articles.title: New GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors Turn GitHub and SharePoint Into Covert C2 Channels
articles.summary: Government sectors in Asia and Africa have been targeted by an active cyber intrusion campaign that delivers to previously undocumented backdoors that leverage legitimate services like Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub for command‑and‑control (C2). The activity has been codenamed Operation ShadowCloud by Kaspersky. The Russian cybersecurity company said it identified the campaign in early 2026.

articles.title: Apple Tightens macOS App Permissions to Limit Data Access Amid AI Agent Security Risks
articles.summary: Apple on Monday introduced new controls that allow Mac users to give more granular access to data they give to apps, including those that use artificial intelligence (AI) agents. The changes, currently previewed in macOS 27.3 beta 2, relate to increased transparency and more options for two of its APIs: Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access. articles.title: Hijacked Optimizely Scripts Served Card Skimmer and iOS Exploit Kits to CNN, BBC and Zoom Visitors
articles.summary: An attacker exploited a flaw in Optimizely Web Experimentation to plant malicious code in some of the scripts that customers' websites load from the service, Optimizely said early today. Visitors to sites run by at least 178 organizations, including CNN, the BBC and Zoom, received the code yesterday, according to Report URI, a firm that monitors the scripts websites run. articles.title: Critical Java4Shell flaw allows RCE attacks on major Java applications
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability dubbed Java4Shell in OpenJDK, the open-source implementation of Java, can allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on popular enterprise applications, including Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak. [...]

articles.title: Cloud keys leaked in Docker Hub images are stolen within seconds
articles.summary: Credentials and access secrets exposed in public Docker Hub images are being extracted and exploited by attackers within as little as eight seconds of publication. [...]

articles.title: Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offlline after cyberattack
articles.summary: The Fugaku supercomputer operated by Japan's RIKEN Center for Computational Science has been taken offline following a security breach. [...]

articles.title: Apple reports outages affecting iCloud Mail, AppleCare and more
articles.summary: Apple is reporting service disruptions affecting several of its services, including iCloud Mail, iCloud Account & Sign In, Apple School Manager, and Schoolwork. [...]

articles.title: Researchers hijack Hugging Face account for popular Kokoro AI model
articles.summary: A Lack of ownership verification on the Hugging Face platform allowed researchers to take control of Kokoro, a text-to-speech model used in projects from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Amazon Web Services. [...]

articles.title: Tor releases emergency update amid ongoing DDoS attack
articles.summary: The Tor Project has released a security update for its network relay software to increase defenses against an ongoing distributed denial-of-service attack that it says has overwhelmed relays and affected most operators. [...]

articles.title: Flipper Devices launches $399 ‘Flipper One’ Linux-based multi-tool
articles.summary: Flipper Devices, the company behind the popular Flipper Zero pentesting device, has launched a crowdfunding campaign for Flipper One, a portable Linux computer and networking multi-tool. [...]

articles.title: Inside Modern Phishing Kits Built to Steal Microsoft 365 Sessions
articles.summary: Huntress researchers break down how EvilTokens, Knight Office, and Kali365 capture and replay M365 tokens, plus how defenders can detect and contain them. [...]

articles.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
articles.summary: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

articles.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

articles.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
articles.summary: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

articles.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
articles.summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices

articles.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
articles.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

articles.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
articles.summary: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
articles.summary: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

articles.title: Optimizely Malware Attacks Highlight Third-Party Vendor Risks
articles.summary: At least 178 organizations, including several major brands, unwittingly exposed website visitors to hydra-like malware via a third-party platform.

articles.title: 'TheMailer' Phishing Kit Puts AI in the Driver's Seat
articles.summary: The commercial kit uses attacker-supplied AI models to personalize lures, evade spam filters, and scale campaigns to tens of thousands of targets.

articles.title: Cursor Traces Malicious Claude Code Extension to Third-Party Breach
articles.summary: A compromised key issued to AI infrastructure provider Fireworks was used by threat actors to access Cursor data and credentials.

articles.title: Grok Bots Attempt to Access Corporate Data Without User Approval
articles.summary: Two AI agents, separately over a five-day period, autonomously tried to access connected applications, including Google Calendar, Gmail, Slack, and GitHub, without account owner approval.

articles.title: Google Project Zero Slashes Bug Disclosure Deadlines, Splitting Experts
articles.summary: One of the oldest running bug disclosure programs announced it would shorten public disclosure timelines to vendors from 120 days to 30 over the next 14 months.

articles.title: Ransomware Attacks Increase Behind AI, but Payments Decline
articles.summary: Large language models and other AI systems allow a growing number of ransomware groups to create convincing phishing emails and identify sensitive data quickly.

articles.title: 'Sleeper Agent' Tactic Hides Payloads in Open-Weight AI Models
articles.summary: Malware can lurk inside just 0.00001% of a neural network. How, then, can any user tell it's there?

articles.title: China-Nexus Actors Breach 10 Organizations in AI-Driven Attacks
articles.summary: Attackers used Cairn once again in autonomous attacks that targeted advanced manufacturing and defense sectors, as well as civil and human rights organizations.

articles.summary: Card numbers, CVVs, expiration dates, and email addresses used at Fandango’s ticketing checkout over four days in October may have been exposed. The post Fandango Warns Ticket Buyers of Payment Card Data Exposure appeared first on SecurityWeek .

articles.summary: More than 40 servers received over 688,000 requests exploiting CVE-2026-84869 to execute guest-pushed files. The post MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign appeared first on SecurityWeek .

articles.title: Access Dental Management Data Breach Impacts Over 340,000
articles.summary: Hackers breached Access Dental’s network and stole personal, health, and insurance information. The post Access Dental Management Data Breach Impacts Over 340,000 appeared first on SecurityWeek .

articles.summary: Led by NEA and supported by existing investors, the funding brings the company’s valuation to $1 billion. The post Corma Receives $125 Million to Train Foundation Models for Defensive Cybersecurity appeared first on SecurityWeek .

articles.title: Student Loan Breach Exposes 2.5M Records
articles.summary: 2.5 million people were affected, in a breach that could spell more trouble down the line.

articles.title: Watering Hole Attacks Push ScanBox Keylogger
articles.summary: Researchers uncover a watering hole attack likely carried out by APT TA423, which attempts to plant the ScanBox JavaScript-based reconnaissance tool.

articles.title: Tentacles of ‘0ktapus’ Threat Group Victimize 130 Firms
articles.summary: Over 130 companies tangled in sprawling phishing campaign that spoofed a multi-factor authentication system.

articles.title: Ransomware Attacks are on the Rise
articles.summary: Lockbit is by far this summer’s most prolific ransomware group, trailed by two offshoots of the Conti group.

articles.title: Cybercriminals Are Selling Access to Chinese Surveillance Cameras
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of cameras have failed to patch a critical, 11-month-old CVE, leaving thousands of organizations exposed.

articles.title: Twitter Whistleblower Complaint: The TL;DR Version
articles.summary: Twitter is blasted for security and privacy lapses by the company’s former head of security who alleges the social media giant’s actions amount to a national security risk.

articles.summary: CISA is warning that Palo Alto Networks’ PAN-OS is under active attack and needs to be patched ASAP.

articles.title: Fake Reservation Links Prey on Weary Travelers
articles.summary: Fake travel reservations are exacting more pain from the travel weary, already dealing with the misery of canceled flights and overbooked hotels.
